newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MEINL PLANS TO GRAB BIGGER MARKET SHARE.
newsitem.headline: MEINL PLANS TO GRAB BIGGER MARKET SHARE.

text.p: Hungarian food retailer chain Csemege-Julius Meinl Rt said on Friday it plans to further boost its Hungarian market share by opening new retail outlets and restructuring its product range according to demand.
"We plan a gross sales of 73.2 billion forints for the full year, an increase of 40.7 percent over last year," Meinl said in its earnings report published in the official bourse gazette.
The company also said it plans to further streamline its operations by continuously upgrading its data processing system.
Meinl said it expected a 2.1 percent reduction in its operating margin.
"The (margin) reduction reflects a below-inflation price increase and the rising proportion of sales in our discount chain Jeee and the C+C chain," the company said.

In the first half of 1997, Meinl posted a group net profit of 392.5 million forints on net sales of 25.3 billion forints compared with a net profit of 430.7 million forints on net sales of 19.66 billion forints in the same period of 1996.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, Meinl shares closed at 14,300 forints on August 11, the last day they were traded.
